data.name: Metro Exodus
data.detailed_description:
• Se tiveres o Metro Exodus também tens direito à Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition, uma atualização visual incrível que REQUER um GPU capaz de apresentar traçados de raios como parte das especificações mínimas.
  • O DLC de Metro Exodus também foi melhorado. Adquirir o Metro Exodus Expansion Pass ou The Two Colonels / Sam's Story individualmente dá-te acesso às versões melhoradas desses conteúdos através da Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition.

Metro Exodus

Estamos em 2036.

25 anos depois de a guerra nuclear ter devastado o planeta, alguns milhares de sobreviventes continuam a agarrar-se à vida por baixo das ruínas de Moscovo, nos túneis do Metro.

Lutaram contra o ambiente envenenado, enfrentaram bestas mutantes e terrores paranormais e sofreram com as chamas da guerra civil.

Mas agora, na pele de Artyom, tens de fugir do Metro e liderar um grupo de Patrulheiros Espartanos numa incrível aventura pelo continente, através de uma Rússia pós-apocalíptica, em busca de uma nova vida no Leste.

Metro Exodus é um jogo épico de tiros na primeira pessoa da 4A Games que combina furtividade e combate letais com exploração e terror de sobrevivência, num dos universos de jogo mais envolventes.

Explora o interior selvagem russo por níveis vastos e não-lineares e acompanha uma emocionante história, que se estende por um ano inteiro, passando pela primavera, pelo verão e pelo outono e terminando no coração do inverno nuclear.

Inspirado nas obras de Dmitry Glukhovsky, Metro Exodus dá continuação à história de Artyom na maior aventura Metro de sempre.

Destaques

  • Entra numa viagem incrível - Embarca na Aurora, uma locomotiva a vapor altamente modificada, e junta-te a outros sobreviventes na busca por uma nova vida no Leste.
  • Vive a sobrevivência em sandbox - Uma história emocionante que liga a jogabilidade clássica de Metro com novos, vastos e incríveis níveis não-lineares.
  • Um mundo belo e hostil - Descobre o interior selvagem russo pós-apocalíptico, animado com ciclos de dia e noite deslumbrantes e clima dinâmico.
  • Furtividade e combate letais - Vasculha o campo e fabrica para personalizar o teu arsenal de armas artesanais e enfrenta inimigos humanos e mutantes em combate tático emocionante.
  • As tuas escolhas determinam o destino dos teus camaradas - Nem todos os teus companheiros vão sobreviver à aventura. As tuas decisões têm consequências nesta narrativa fascinante que te incita a jogar vezes sem conta.
  • O melhor em atmosfera e imersão - Uma vela tremeluzente na escuridão; um suspiro ofegante, enquanto a tua máscara de gás se embacia; o uivo de um mutante levado pelo vento da noite — vais mergulhar em Metro e ser aterrorizado como em nenhum outro jogo...

data.short_description: Foge das ruínas do Metro de Moscovo e embarca numa aventura épica pelo continente, através do interior selvagem russo pós-apocalíptico. Explora níveis vastos e não-lineares, mergulha numa experiência de sobrevivência em sandbox e acompanha uma emocionante história que se estende por um ano inteiro na maior aventura Metro de sempre.

reviews.review:
[h2]TLDR:[/h2] An intriguing evolution of the Metro formula with excellent gameplay and a well-paced story, undermined by discouraging technical issues.

[h2]GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW:[/h2] Metro Exodus is a survival horror game with heavy FPS elements. The player once again takes on the role of Artyom, one of several thousand survivors in the Moscow metro after a nuclear war.

Exodus plays in first person. As in previous games, Artyom is a silent protagonist, save narrating between chapters. The game proceeds in a (mostly) linear fashion, following Artyom's journey out of Moscow and across a ruined Russian landscape by train. The player can carry up to three weapons (two in the highest difficulty), ammo, healing kits, grenades, and so on. Armor and guns can be upgraded with various enhancements found during the adventure.

This game adds a crafting element to the series. The player will find two resources: materials and chemicals. Together, these allow the player to build certain items—such as healing kits and gas mask canisters—through their backpack interface. Ammo and grenades can also be crafted at workbenches. Weapon maintenance is a factor. The player's guns collect grime and dirt through use and eventually can seize if not cleaned at the workbench using chemical resources. Amounts of crafting supplies found vary by difficulty. On the easiest mode, the player will be swimming in resources, while on the harder difficulties, players will have to make difficult decisions about what items are really needed. Difficulty also affects how much ammo is found, meaning players must account for every round fired.

Players can tackle enemy encounters by going in with guns blazing or sneaking through. Combat can be fast and intense, but is satisfying. Weapon handling generally feels pretty good and as new weapons are found, copies are stored on the train, so the player can usually tailor their loadout before setting out.

In my opinion, combat is a bit less forgiving than in previous Metro games. For one, in many areas, it is possible to alert upward of a dozen foes, which is almost certain death. A few late-game brutes are relatively easy to avoid but do nightmarish damage, all but one-shotting the player on higher difficulties. The game also features a handful of difficult fights—either with bosses or against large numbers of opponents—that cannot be skipped or avoided. Outside those encounters, stealth is a viable option in most situations; in fact, stealth is almost a mandatory part of play on Normal or higher, to avoid as many of the dangerous brawls as possible, with resource scarcity being an issue.

Much is made of Exodus moving the franchise to a more "open-world" environment but of the six major zones, only two are truly open, with the rest being relatively linear. Traversal over the zones includes a lot of vehicle travel on boats and in one chapter, a van. Vehicle handling is a little clunky but I felt the awkward movement of dilapidated boats and vans accurately reflects the decayed condition of everything.

Artyom has a whole pack of companions on his journey. Player actions have a lasting impact on the fate of several of them, and possibly the player's own ending. Exodus employs the same "morality" system of previous games, where the screen gives a light white flash on a good moral action. Good actions are what one might expect, such as sparing enemies, freeing prisoners from bandits, etc. A player pretty much has to avoid killing anyone who doesn't deserve it to make it to the good ending. If seeking that good ending, I recommend listening to your companions and NPCs as to whom to spare.

All in all, the mechanics of the game blend together into something entertaining and stressful at the same time. I spent a lot of playtime on the edge of my seat, waiting for something to go horribly wrong. I started worrying about the fate of my companions, which is a good measure of a game's ability to draw in and captivate a player. On that count, Exodus is an unqualified success.

[h2]STORY / WORLDBUILDING:[/h2] The tale opens with Artyom obsessed with finding survivors on the surface. Now married to Anna (the sniper from the last game), he is reprimanded for wasting time and resources on dangerous missions, before he and Anna witness a working train shooting across the wasteland. Investigating said train goes wrong, revealing to Artyom that much of what they'd been told was a lie. Eventually his whole squad is involved and they escape, taking the train on a crosscountry journey. Along the way, they face feudal warlords, cultists, and some other surprises. Several characters find their expectations and hopes undercut, face their disillusionment, and move on to focus on their future. The whole narrative is pretty captivating.

The grim setting builds on that of the first two games, though it mostly exchanges the filthy, claustrophobic tunnels of the subway system for a ruined and irradiated surface. Years of neglect following the war have left buildings in a state of disrepair and cars nothing but rusted hulks. Aqueducts and industrial pumps have failed, leaving basements and low-lying areas flooded. The overall sense of decay is well-represented, adding to the game's despair and depression. I enjoyed the story and world but it was enough of a downer that I also had to take breaks from it.

[h2]DLC:[/h2] This version of Exodus includes two DLCs, Two Colonels and Sam's Story. The former tells a backstory for a character Artyom meets along the way, while the latter is an adventure for one of Artyom's companions set after the main game ends. Each DLC features an interesting scenario, though both are pretty linear and involve challenging mandatory fights. Together, the two add 8-10 hours of gameplay.

[h2]TECHNICAL ASPECTS:[/h2] Exodus looks and feels great. Visuals are dark and grimy, befitting the ruined world. Character models are detailed and animations are excellent. I enjoyed the sound design, and the varied (by region) ambient sound generally adds to an area's uneasy feeling. Voice acting is decent too.

This excellent presentation is badly marred by pervasive instability. I had numerous crashes that not only froze the game but hardlocked my entire system. Disabling overlays, updating drivers, and other suggested fixes were unsuccessful. Using GPU software to lock myself to 60 FPS cut down the number of crashes but didn't eliminate them altogether. I expect most people would find this an unreasonable solution. Corrupted files and lost save data occurred about every other time I started the game.

Aside from those serious concerns, Exodus has many minor problems, such as mistimed dialogue lines or characters speaking over each other. In one section, I had enemies lock me in combat (meaning no saves) from across the map and I wasn't able to unlock without returning to deal with them. I had collectibles that refused to appear, even on restarting the game or replaying the chapter. A demon picked me up and dropped me clear out of the world, as shown:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3823555274

If a player uses a map while driving the van, their field of vision sometimes reorients in the ceiling. Exiting the vehicle and reentering seems to be the only way to fix it. All of these issues were frequent and persistent enough to detract from my overall enjoyment.

Steam achievements will require several full runs through the game to get alternate endings, including on high difficulty and "iron man" mode (saves only allowed between chapters), and finding all collectibles.

[h2]FINAL WORD:[/h2] I enjoyed Metro enough to play through it twice and get each ending. I'd consider revisiting it, if I thought I could stomach the constant instability.
